notes:
Adversarial comparison run at matched scale via a side-by-side composite of the blueprint collar region against the same region of candidate-1. Actively looked for grounds to reject and found none that block.

CONFIRMED MATCHES. Orientation: both are detail close-ups of the collar/neckline at the same three-quarter camera angle - correct face of the garment, no front/back confusion. Feature counts are exact: 2 collar leaves (2/2), 2 collar points (2/2), 1 throat button (1/1), 1 visible placket button (1/1), 1 row of collar edge topstitching (1/1). Placement of the throat button is the decisive check and it is right: in both images the button sits immediately to the right of the left leaf's inner corner, on the small neckband tab, at the same relative height - it is a THROAT button per the catalog text ('a throat button that fastens the leaves neatly together'), NOT a button-down collar button anchoring the points to the body, and the photo did not drift into that far more common convention. Point geometry: measured at matched scale the left leaf's fold-apex-to-point length is 0.503 of the crop height in the photo vs 0.505 in the blueprint, and the point angle and lower-edge slope are visually indistinguishable. Construction: single-needle straight topstitch in both - critically NOT the decorative zigzag belonging to sibling option collar-point-58-zigzag, so no neighbouring-option contamination. No generic spread/semi-spread collar substituted for the drawn point.

Composition and cleanliness: the collar occupies roughly 45-50% of the frame, within the 40-80% dominance target, is unobstructed, and is identifiable in under a second. Background is a plain seamless neutral light-grey with no location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props. Scanned the full frame at boosted contrast including all four corners - no text, no numbers, no units, no leader or dimension lines, no arrows, no coloured guide marks, no ruler ticks, no watermark. Result is photographic, not line-art or CGI.

The only deviations found are the three minors logged above; none of them would cause a customer to misidentify this option or confuse it with any sibling.
